channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Slovakia: PM Robert Fico's NATO Article 5 remarks spark criticism and raise questions about his country's NATO commitment
item.description: Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico says he fears war and will do everything he can to keep his country out of one. Critics say his remarks risk weakening NATO, the alliance that was designed to prevent such a war.

item.title: [Financial Times] Trump praises ‘tremendous self-regulation’ of AI after summoning tech bosses to the White House
item.description: President says chief executives have signed a ‘morally binding’ accord after lunch with industry leaders

item.title: [Financial Times] Altman says OpenAI will delay its IPO until it overcomes safety concerns
item.description: ChatGPT maker launches a new AI personal assistant as it faces a challenge from Meta’s Muse

item.title: [Financial Times] Hegseth to slash top US military officer roles by 20%
item.description: Generals’ and admirals’ positions will be cut as part of the defence secretary’s wide-ranging overhaul of the armed services

item.title: [Financial Times] Suspect in RAF Fairford incident called 999 shortly before arrest
item.description: Motive for the emergency call is unclear, as police continue to investigate incident at air base used by US bombers

item.title: [Financial Times] US 30-year Treasury yield hits highest since 2002
item.description: Government debt extends decline as inflation and surging oil prices weigh on market

item.title: [Politico Europe] Bruxelles veut clarifier les responsabilités des autorités face aux catastrophes climatiques
item.description: La nouvelle proposition de la Commission européenne cherchera à préciser qui, des autorités nationales ou locales, est chargé de gérer les feux de forêt et les inondations.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tax cuts, handouts and blind hope: Europe finds few tools to fight a coming energy crunch
item.description: European energy ministers gathered in Dublin had limited new ideas to protect against a winter of soaring power bills.

item.title: [Financial Times] Man City found to have artificially boosted finances by more than £900mn
item.description: Independent commission said Premier League football club arranged ‘sham’ commercial deals to disguise sources of funding

item.title: [Politico Europe] Burnham tried to plot the next 7 years of UK politics in one speech
item.description: Four issues — Europe, electoral reform, social care and public sector pensions — towered over the rest in the U.K. leader's first speech to conference.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Greek opposition jabs ruling party over reported threats from Trump’s envoy
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle has caused a stir in Athens and Bucharest.

item.title: [EU Observer] Frugal EU states seeking budget cuts are shooting their own regions in the foot
item.description: Despite joining a frugal ultimatum for EU budget cuts, the Dutch get roughly as much growth from EU investment as they pay in, while narrowing the gap between wealthier and poorer regions.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Merz says Lavrov comments show Moscow not interested in serious negotiations
item.description: The chancellor’s remarks come days after a surprise meeting between Russia’s foreign minister and his German counterpart.

item.title: [EU Observer] Former MEP Rachida Dati’s 2014 emails derided corruption allegations, which now form core of French trial
item.description: Former French MEP and culture minister Rachida Dati, who is now a Paris mayor, threatened to sue EUobserver in 2014 emails about corruption allegations, which are now coming home to roost in high-profile French trails.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK energy infrastructure under constant threat, minister warns
item.description: It is a "really scary world," Michael Shanks told Labour's annual conference.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Andy Burnham keeps his options open on Brexit
item.description: The U.K. prime minister said he would lay out different paths for the future EU relationship at a summit later this year.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Interdiction des exportations de diesel : Trump devrait y renoncer, positivent des responsables européens
item.description: Selon le ministre irlandais de l’Energie, Darragh O’Brien, il “ne semble pas” que cette menace “risque de se produire”.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU countries push for weaker environmental safeguards in fishing sector funding rules
item.description: The move sets up a fight with the Commission over the treatment of fisheries in the EU budget.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs vote for €47bn in new Erasmus+ funds, as frugal states seek cuts to EU budget
item.description: With 24 votes in favour and one abstention, MEPs proposed to increase the European Commission's original proposal from €40bn to €47bn on Tuesday.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Dans les coulisses de la fin du macronisme
item.description: La droite et le centre apparaissent plus faibles que jamais au sortir des deux mandats d’Emmanuel Macron. Quelle responsabilité porte le président dans l’état de déliquescence de son propre camp ? Pauline Thiévenaud, journaliste à RTL, et Jérémy Marot, journaliste à l’AFP, ont mené 160 entretiens et racontent dans « Le crépuscule des princes », […]

item.title: [EU Observer] EU’s centre-right EPP seeks asylum opt-outs, as commission silent on new crisis rules
item.description: Political pressure for allowing EU asylum opt-outs continues to increase, as commission drafts vague new emergency rules in the wake of this summer's Ceuta episode.

item.title: [EU Observer] Scientists flee burning building in Kyiv’s mini-9/11, as Russian drone also explodes 200m from EU embassy (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,678)
item.description: Despite global audiences being numbed to daily Kyiv airstrikes and casualties, Russia's 9/11-type attack on a scientific institute, in a botched assassination attempt, still grabbed world attention.

item.title: [DW] UK PM Burnham seeks 'hope again' at Labour Party conference
item.description: Andy Burnham is seeking a delicate balance between optimism and realism at Labour's annual party conference. He promised hope and an end to "politics as usual" but also an "honest conversation" about difficult dilemmas.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU reduces funds for women’s rights groups, in wider budget bonfire of good causes
item.description: As the EU seeks budget cuts to break a stalemate in member states' talks, women's rights groups are on the chopping bloc, prompting advocates' concern that important causes are fading from the common agenda.

item.title: [DW] Albania: As corruption cases multiply, experts question whether the anti-corruption drive is addressing the causes or just the symptoms.
item.description: From a former president to the ex-intelligence chief, Albania is prosecuting senior officials at a rate once thought impossible. But do more prosecutions mean less corruption or simply better enforcement?

item.title: [Financial Times] A Republican midterm defeat will not be an earthquake
item.description: Democrats are likely to make gains in Congress but divided government is unlikely to derail Trump’s agenda

item.title: [EU Observer] Private money follows profit, not ruins in Ukraine’s EU-backed reconstruction
item.description: Internal financing data, loan records, and investment flows reveal how European promises to “rebuild Ukraine” quietly sidestep the utilities, housing, and local firms in Ukraine’s battered eastern and frontline regions, while capital concentrates in Kyiv and the safer west.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Can EU countries agree on the next long-term budget?
item.description: The EU is negotiating its next long-term budget as countries discuss possible new taxes directly to the EU budget or, on the contrary, funding cuts.

item.title: [DW] UK: US government questions bail for Fairford base suspects
item.description: The US government sees "the hand of a foreign actor" in the security scare at RAF Fairford, a hub for US heavy bombers in Europe. Donald Trump criticized the suspects being released on bail amid ongoing investigations.

item.title: [EU Observer] From Munich to Prešov and Leipzig: a GRU-linked sabotage network operated from Slovak territory
item.description: Slovakia has become a staging ground for Russian operations. A bad news meaning Europe’s defence industry, airports and supply lines to Ukraine can be targeted far from the actual front line.

item.title: [Financial Times] Nvidia turns to insurers to spread the risk of AI build-out
item.description: World’s largest listed company looks for new ways to draw Wall Street deeper into the financing of the AI boom

item.title: [Financial Times] Bond investors become oil traders as Iran war drives yields
item.description: Bond investors watch Iran conflict and crude price for signs as to where government borrowing costs will go

item.title: [Financial Times] Starbucks scales back ESG goals and fires sustainability staff
item.description: Early corporate champion of climate action scales back or reviews targets to halve emissions, waste and water use

item.title: [DW] Czech PM Andrej Babis reiterates importance of NATO for his country but rejects calls to increase defense spending
item.description: The US and NATO want Czechia to spend more on defense. Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babis says Prague cannot afford faster increases, despite growing warnings about the threat from Russia.

item.title: [DW] 'Pope fever' takes hold as Pope Leo visits France
item.description: Pope Leo XIV is expected to draw huge crowds during his visit to France. As part of his trip, he's also set to address Europe's future and some of the challenges ahead.

item.title: [DW] European cities seek ways of boosting affordable housing
item.description: In many major urban centers of Europe, the housing shortage has become an explosive social issue. DW looks into various models that have been put in place across the continent.

item.title: [DW] Backlash over data centers tests Europe's AI ambitions
item.description: Massive data centers needed to run AI are triggering protests across Europe. Their operators counter that they boost digital sovereignty and energy independence.

item.title: [DW] Russia expected to intensify hybrid war on Europe
item.description: Drone explosions, airspace violations, arson attacks: Poland, Romania, and Moldova are now regularly targeted in Russian attacks against Ukraine. More governments are calling these attacks deliberate acts of aggression.

item.title: [DW] Russian classroom propaganda glorifies dying for your country, students say
item.description: The Russian government has stepped up its efforts to spread patriotic propaganda in schools. DW spoke to students about textbooks that portray the West as hostile and promote sacrifice for the nation.

item.title: [EU Observer] From Yemen to Ethiopia and Europe: Everything is connected
item.description: The EU could easily catch cold from a civil war in Ethiopia that has broken out weeks after the capture of the Yemeni coastline by Houthi rebels. These, and other events in the region, are all connected.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Made in everywhere’: MEPs clash over reach of EU industrial law
item.description: Lead MEPs want 'Made in Europe' perks limited to the 27 member states. The centre-right, whose votes could decide the file, is split.

item.title: [EU Observer] Kallas regrets EU delisting of oligarchs, as Russia ‘ridicules’ Germany after UN meeting
item.description: Swedish defence minister Pål Jonson also said on Monday: "We should increase the price for Russian aggression, and it is only then that Russia will understand that they will not win this war".

item.title: [EU Observer] Munich talks keep EU return‑hub plan alive despite drop in border arrivals and budget questions
item.description: Irregular arrivals to the EU are falling, but the infrastructure of its militarised borders is only getting started. Interior ministers from various member states met in Munich to advance plans to offshore migration processing to third countries.

item.title: [DW] Sicily: Mount Etna ash disrupts Catania flights again
item.description: A thick ash cloud from Mount Etna has been disrupting flights to Catania in Sicily for several days. Italy and Europe's most active volcano, Etna has impacted air travel several times this summer.

item.title: [DW] Turkey: Comedian convicted for 'insulting' Erdogan in show
item.description: Deniz Goktas was convicted of two of three charges, including "insulting" the president, but was released pending the appeal process. Nominally, Turkey is a secular country with free speech.

item.title: [EU Observer] Protesters in Brussels press EU on ‘broken promises’ over caged animals
item.description: Animal rights activists call for the commission to finally table cage ban proposals after years of delays, while Irish Ferries has 15 days to respond to a new complaint about transporting calves without giving them food.

item.title: [EU Observer] Baltic states seek to calm panic on Russia, in role reversal
item.description: Warnings about Russia's escalation against Nato have prompted fear in Europe, but the Baltic states' risk assessments remain unchanged.

item.title: [DW] 'Lithuanian skies are NATO skies': DW speaks with Lithuanian premier Mindaugas Sinkevicius
item.description: In a DW interview, Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius discussed threats to Lithuania from Russia and Belarus, NATO's need for stronger air defense and why military spending alone cannot ensure security.

item.title: [DW] How Bulgaria become a global leader in battery storage and what this means for the country's grid and energy market?
item.description: In under two years, Bulgaria has become one of the world's most battery-intensive energy markets. Can the surge last — and what will it mean for conventional power generators?

item.title: [DW] Italy to ban burqa in schools, limit foreign pupils
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni’s government has passed new school rules capping the number of students who don't speak fluent Italian and banning face coverings.
